target_customer: Software engineering teams (per YC page); environmental professionals doing Phase I ESAs (per current site)
problem: Autonomous coding agents act without clarifying requirements; engineers want to stay in control. Current site: Phase I environmental site assessments are slow desk work.
business_model: SaaS subscription (assumed from product, not confirmed)
product_category: AI coding agent, now AI for environmental due diligence

founders.name: Jonathan Miranda
previous_startups: Hopkins Deliveries campus delivery (outcome not stated)

technical_complexity.rationale: Agent workflow around third-party LLMs (launch lists GLM 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5); standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: A coding-agent workflow is copyable in weeks; Cursor and Claude Code are the autonomous alternatives it positions against.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. The company's own site now omits the coding agent entirely and targets environmental due diligence, consistent with abandoning the wedge, but the reason is not stated.

market_need_then: Founders say they built a demo in days with Claude Code and Cursor and then spent weeks cleaning up code they did not understand (YC launch post, company claim).

identity.visual_style: Bold headings, numbered feature blocks, document-like mockups (company site).
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct, short declarative headlines with some wit (company site).

branding.community_and_virality: Several Product Hunt launches under changing taglines (Oct 10, Oct 19, Nov 8 2025); no evidence of community pull.

brand_strength.rationale: No source on brand strength found; not rated.

pivots.from: AI coding agent that asks before it acts (YC page, Oct-Nov 2025 launches)
pivots.to: AI platform for Environmental Due Diligence / Phase I ESAs (compyle.ai, 2026-11)

outcome_analysis: Compyle (Fall 2025, Active) launched a coding agent in October and November 2025 and by November 2026 its site describes only environmental due diligence automation, so the coding-agent wedge appears to have been dropped within about a year. The reason is not public; the crowded market against Cursor and Claude Code is a plausible but unsourced factor, so no failure factors are asserted.
